In Communications Technology, fabrication serves a message and audience. Students should justify hierarchy, typography, colour, media choice, viewing conditions, accessibility, copyright, and production workflow, not only make a decorative object.

## Project directions

:::: {.ter-project-grid}
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Accessible tabletop wayfinding system
<p class="ter-course-code">TGJ2O · Display family</p>
Create a coordinated sign family for a real school event with readable hierarchy, consistent arrows, and stable supports.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Audience study → information architecture → vector system → prototype → distance test</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Typography, contrast, symbols, layout, fabrication setup</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate · three related signs</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Cardboard test; approved sheet stock or print substrate for final</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Base must resist a bump and preserve sign angle</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>Do not obstruct exits; verify event and accessibility requirements</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=communications-technology&type=project-components">Sign and stand components</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../02-digital-design/04-layout-typography-colour.qmd">Layout, Type & Colour</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Create print, fabricated, and mobile-screen versions of the same system</dd></dl>
:::
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Repeatable product-photo jig
<p class="ter-course-code">TGJ2O / senior TGJ · Gauge / fixture family</p>
Build a fixture that repeats camera, product, and background position for before/after or catalogue photography.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Shot requirements → datum layout → fixture → image series → variation review</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Composition, lighting control, repeatability, file workflow</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Intermediate · desktop setup</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Matte board, plywood, or printed brackets</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>Stabilize devices without blocking controls or ventilation</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>Secure stands and route cables to prevent trips</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=communications-technology&type=jigs-gauges">Positioning and angle references</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../01-nice-design-process/04-prototype-evaluate-iterate.qmd">Prototype, Evaluate & Iterate</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Measure visual consistency across a ten-image batch</dd></dl>
:::
::: {.ter-project-card}
### Modular exhibit or prop system
<p class="ter-course-code">Senior TGJ · Portable work module</p>
Develop a flat-pack display or non-load-bearing prop with replaceable message panels and a documented assembly sequence.
<dl><dt>Process</dt><dd>Creative brief → thumbnails → scale model → joint test → full prototype</dd><dt>Skills</dt><dd>Brand system, story, joinery, exploded view, production plan</dd><dt>Difficulty / size</dt><dd>Advanced · transportable by one student</dd><dt>Material</dt><dd>Corrugated sheet, plywood, print media, or textile skin</dd><dt>Structural</dt><dd>State load limits; protect against tipping and panel release</dd><dt>Safety</dt><dd>No overhead, climbing, flame-effect, or life-safety use</dd><dt>Library</dt><dd><a href="../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?technology=communications-technology&type=themed-starters">Original design starters</a></dd><dt>Lesson</dt><dd><a href="../../03-laser-cutting/05-assemblies-hybrid-fabrication.qmd">Assemblies + Hybrid Fabrication</a></dd><dt>Extension</dt><dd>Publish a mini brand guide and accessible digital companion</dd></dl>
:::
::::
